findings.summary: Code run by Run can still escape the new confinement: it may write the tree's own `.git`, and eddy later runs git in that tree without confinement, which runs whatever the planted git config names.
findings.detail: `running_reviewed` lets Run (and rust-analyzer, which runs build scripts) write all of `scratchpad/eddy-tree`, including the tree's `.git` file. eddy itself runs git inside that tree with no grants, as the guest: `reset_snapshot`/`reset_checkout` (`git reset --hard`, `git clean -ffdx`) after a reproduction in report.wado and after each baseline run, `patch_of`, and now `checkout_at` (`git -C <tree> checkout --force`) at the start of the next review, since the tree is no longer removed and is reused whenever `.git` exists in it. The reviewed code can swap that `.git` file for a directory, or point its `gitdir:` at a repository it controls, whose config sets `core.fsmonitor` or `core.hooksPath` (for example a `post-checkout` hook). git runs that command with eddy's own access: write access to the developer's whole checkout and its real `.git`. That is the access the commit says Run no longer has ('the developer's checkout and its .git ... which eddy then runs git in'). The same applies to the build submodule worktrees inside the tree. Because the tree now persists between runs, a tree tampered with in one review is used without question by the next run's `checkout_at`. Not reproduced: every child spawn in this sandbox fails with NotPermitted, including in the existing core:process tests, so neither git nor the confined Run could be run here. The bypass follows from the grants (write access to the whole tree, `.git` included) and from the unconfined `tree_git` calls on that tree.
